headline: Mariana has lost 8% of her body weight (77.9 to 71.7 kg) from Sep 5 to Nov 24, 2026, and her son and primary caregiver reports exhaustion and has asked for respite; a Nov 26 chart correction disputes the weight-loss note.

items.statement: Weight fell steadily from 77.9 kg (Sep 5) to 75.7 kg (Oct 1), 73.6 kg (Oct 28) and 71.7 kg (Nov 24), a loss of 6.2 kg (8.0%). On Nov 24 the dietitian documented poor appetite, skipped breakfast and about 50% of day center lunches eaten. The plan was an oral nutrition supplement twice daily, weekly weights and a dental check for chewing problems.
items.verifier_note: The weights, dates, 6.2 kg (8.0%) loss, and the Nov 24 dietitian findings and plan all match the vitals record and note n002.

items.statement: On Sep 27 the social worker met with Marcus, her son and primary caregiver. He reported exhaustion, poor sleep and worry about managing evenings alone, and requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed.
items.verifier_note: Note n001 matches every detail: Sep 27 social worker meeting, Marcus as son and primary caregiver, exhaustion, poor sleep, worry about evenings alone, respite request, and the discussion of respite options and a support group.

items.statement: A Nov 26 chart correction, attributed to Dr. Nakamura, says the Nov 24 weight-loss entry was documented on the wrong participant and should be disregarded. The structured weight record independently shows the 4 readings and the 8% decline for Mariana. The original event is reported as documented, and the conflict needs resolving.

questions: Which record is correct: the Nov 26 correction saying the Nov 24 weight note belongs to another participant, or the vitals record showing a steady decline for Mariana? Can the weights be verified and the correction source confirmed?
Should the dietitian's plan (supplement twice daily, weekly weights, dental check) go ahead while the conflict is resolved?
